title: Kitab al-Hujja 'ala Ahl al-Madina
altTitles: The Argument against the People of Medina
author: al-shaybani
attributionNote: The attribution is the one the manuscript tradition and the scholarship give.
description: Al-Shaybani sets the doctrine of Abu Hanifa beside that of the Medinan jurists on point after point, states where they differ, and argues for the Kufan position from hadith, the reports of the Companions and analogy. It is the earliest surviving work devoted to the disagreement between the schools.
historicalContext: Written after al-Shaybani's years with Malik in Medina, the book shows the two great centres of early Islamic law arguing with one another before the schools hardened. It is a primary witness to how legal reasoning was conducted in the eighth century.
availabilityNote: Arabic text only, streamed from OpenITI at read time. No English translation is included because no public-domain English translation was verified. Only the catalogue record, chapter outline and passage index are held here.
